etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English importen, from Old French emporter, importer, from Latin importō (“bring in from abroad, import”, verb), from in (“in, at, on; into”) + portō (“I carry, bear; convey”).

definitions.definition: (countable) Something brought in from an exterior source, especially for sale or trade.

quote.citation: 2023 December 27, Christian Wolmar, “Hope springs eternal for greater use of the Channel Tunnel”, in RAIL, number 999, page 26:
quote.text: There is, too, a little mentioned aspect of the tunnel which contributes to its failings. You never see the sea while approaching it from either the British or French side. That takes away from the import of the journey - a historic link between Britain and the continent. Instead, it is just a tunnel.

definitions.definition: (countable, Philippines) A foreigner playing in a sports league.
(transitive) To bring (something) in from a foreign country, especially for sale or trade.
(transitive, computing) To load a file into a software application from another version or system.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Italian importare, and French importer, from Latin importō.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To be important; to be significant; to be of consequence.

quote.citation: 1661, Thomas Salusbury, (Please provide the book title or journal name):
quote.text: See how much it importeth to learn to take Time by the Fore-Top.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To be of importance to (someone or something).

quote.text: This Letter is mistooke: it importeth none here: It is writ to laquenetta.

quote.citation: 1681, John Dryden, The Spanish Fryar: Or, the Double Discovery. […], London:  […]  Richard Tonson and Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC, (please specify the page number):
quote.text: If I endure it, what imports it you?

definitions.definition: (transitive) To be incumbent on (someone to do something).

quote.citation: 1762, David Hume, The History of England:
quote.text: It imports us to get all the aid and assistance we can.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To be important or crucial to (that something happen).

quote.text: It much imports your house That all should be made clear.

quote.citation: 1594–1597, Richard Hooker, edited by J[ohn] S[penser], Of the Lawes of Ecclesiastical Politie, […], London:  […]  Will[iam] Stansby [for Matthew Lownes], published 1611, →OCLC, (please specify the page):
quote.text: Every petition  […]  doth  […]  always import a multitude of speakers together.
